3: The tasting rooms taught this town to try before committing, and a great room that hosts deserves the same. So the showroom comes here instead — 20+ carpet samples, and pad in all three grades, unrolled in the room they would actually cover. We measure the stairs, the guest rooms, every corner of it, and the written price is in your hands before the van pulls out.
19: once the pad, labor, new tack strip, haul-away and the carpet itself are all added together. Two Woodinville numbers to hold onto: most jobs finish between $2,000 and $4,500, and a 1,200 sq ft main level with a staircase generally lands at $5,500–$8,500. What moves it is grade. You settle that question in your own great room, samples on the subfloor, rather than off a photo on a screen.
23: All three pad grades plus 20+ carpet samples, laid out room by room
54: Two phone pictures do it — the wrinkle up close, then the whole room from the doorway. Send them in and an estimator writes back the same business day with a verdict and a price: $99 stretch, or replacement. No one has to drive up Hollywood Hill for it, and no one rings you afterward to sell.
67: A whole Woodinville project — great room, stairs, the guest bedrooms — usually finishes between $2,000 and $4,500. Take a 1,200 sq ft main level plus that staircase and it runs more like $5,500 to $8,500. Per square foot installed that is $4 to $7, with carpet, pad, labor, tack strip and haul-away inside the figure. Grade is the variable, and you set it with samples down on your own floor.
69: Hollywood Hill, English Hill, and the Sammamish Valley floor where the tasting rooms sit — all of it is on the route, and the visit costs nothing. The van carries all three pad grades and 20+ carpet samples. Those get laid down in the rooms being recarpeted, so you judge color under your own windows instead of store lighting. We measure every room and every stair tread, then write out the price before pulling away.
71: $99 per room is where stretching starts in Woodinville. A power stretcher pulls the slack out — ripples along a hallway, the wave that curls up and catches a heel before company arrives — for roughly a fifth of new carpet. So long as the fiber has not gone flat and the color still belongs in the house, that is the better place to spend.
79: Four things settle it, and we check all four before writing a quote: does the pile spring back, is the backing still holding together, are seams opening, and did a professional cleaning actually end the pet odor. Clear those and it is a $99-per-room stretch. Miss them — lanes crushed flat through the great room, backing coming apart — and the carpet has earned a replacement.
83: Start with the pad. The moisture-barrier grade, which starts at $0.65 per square foot, is what does the real work: odor only turns permanent after a mess soaks through to the subfloor, and the barrier stops it there. Over that, solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing. The color is locked into the fiber, so a diluted-bleach cleanup will not lighten it — which matters in a house where the dogs greet every guest at the door.
85: Two warranties, not one. Labor is ours for a year — OC Flooring's workmanship coverage, printed on the quote. The carpet's own mill warranty comes from the manufacturer, typically 10 to 25 years against wear and stains depending on grade. One catch: some mills void that coverage below a certain pad grade, which matters on stairs and in a great room that hosts, so all three grades are on board when we measure.
